backend.title: What an idempotency key actually does
backend.describe: A client sends a transfer request. The server debits the sender, credits the receiver, commits, and starts writing the response. The connection drops half a millisecond before the client reads it. The client, seeing no response, does the only reasonable thing a retry policy knows how to do: sends the same request again. The server has no idea any of that happened. It just sees a second, perfectly well-formed request to move money. So it does it again.
